clue.text: What's possibly canned talk of circuit training?

indicators.note: training puts a body through drills and reshapes it, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

blocks.note: all thirteen letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A gym instructor chatting about circuit training, wondering if the patter is pre-recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like 'pre-recorded' talk; in the definition it means sold in a tin, which is how fruit cocktail usually comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit cocktail is a mix of chopped fruit typically sold tinned, so it is one example of something canned.

clue.text: International concerns offering safari trips

blocks.note: first meaning: matters of a country's dealings with other nations
second meaning, playful: holidays abroad are literally foreign outings or affairs

explanation.surface: A travel company with global business interests advertises safari holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a safari is an affair (an event) in a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard term for a government's overseas policy and also literally describes events happening abroad.

clue.text: Students' club working to support education facility

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it is written after the other one

blocks.note: short for university
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job to fund their studies, perhaps by working at the bar of the students' club.
explanation.definitionFit: A students' union is the society and building that serves a university's student body, often run like a club.

clue.text: Nick 'er fishing gear from Spooner's tent

anglers call their rods and lines tackle; it takes the first phrase's opening sound

explanation.surface: Someone steals a woman's fishing kit from a man's tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick 'er' means nab her; swap the N and T sounds of 'nab 'er tackle' to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the tabernacle was the portable sanctuary carried by the Israelites, a sacred tent.

clue.text: Virgin commercial plugs every 60 mins on the radio?

explanation.surface: The Virgin brand runs an advert every hour on a radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin is capitalised to pass the Virgin Mary off as Richard Branson's company. The silent H means the hour word starts with a vowel sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Lady is the title Catholics and others use for Mary, the mother of Jesus, known as the Virgin.

clue.text: Look up mother, don't say a word!

blocks.note: to peek is to take a quick look
British for mother

explanation.definitionFit: Keep mum is an idiom ordering someone to stay silent and keep a secret.

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
just the first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Awry means askew or out of line, the same as something bent or crooked.

clue.text: Loth to struggle with a grim topic of a maths class

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: After this broadcast the ratings are bound to go up

definitions.text: After this broadcast the ratings are bound to go up

blocks.clueFragment: After this broadcast the ratings are bound to go up

setter's reading: ratings are ordinary sailors, and a call over the ship's tannoy sends them climbing to the upper level

explanation.walkthrough: Ratings means naval sailors, not audience figures; the broadcast is a shout through a ship telling every crew member to come up top.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a naval order summoning every crew member above to the top level of the ship, now an idiom for an emergency effort.

clue.text: Refund back massage in French city ending in rupture

the final letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back massage' reads as one thing; split it, so 'back' acts on massage alone. Reims is the cathedral city of Champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay money spent, the same as giving a refund.

clue.text: Knocked back Pils like His Majesty?

explanation.definitionFit: Regal means fit for or befitting a king or queen, so it describes royalty.

standard abbreviation

explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are personal and hidden, matching the sense of private.

clue.text: Rounds of ham with the crust removed

clue.text: Principal section of the foot

clue.text: Branch of Anglicanism in which worshippers are closer to God?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: a lofty building would literally bring people closer to a God imagined above.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the Anglican tradition stressing ritual, sacraments and priestly authority, close to Catholic practice.

clue.text: A few translated antonym

clue.text: Like the best chips I saw eaten out

standard abbreviation, as on a tap
the international vehicle code
